thought.text: Single-file bind mount prevents sed's in-place rename. I'll mount a directory instead.

reasoning_content:
Now the mount isn't read-only but the bind mount on a single file causes "Device or resource busy" when sed tries to rename. The osixia startup script tries to sed the custom ldif in place. A single-file bind mount makes sed's rename fail.

Solution: mount the whole directory instead of a single file. Or copy the ldif into a volume. Better: bind mount a directory. The compose mounts `../test_users.ldif` file. Change to mount a directory containing it. But the custom bootstrap ldif dir can have multiple files.

Let me create a directory e.g. `.ddev/ldap-bootstrap/` containing test_users.ldif, and mount that dir to /container/service/slapd/assets/config/bootstrap/ldif/custom. Actually mounting the whole custom dir could hide other image content. Better mount to a subdir? The startup reads custom ldif files from that dir.

Actually osixia's startup script does `sed` on files in the custom dir; mounting a directory volume works fine because the dir is a real mount and rename within it works.

Let me create a directory and copy test_users.ldif there. Mount directory. But the custom dir may already contain files from image (probably empty). Let's do it.

Also LDAP_TLS_VERIFY_CLIENT=demand may cause issues but let's see.

Let me set up.

action.command:
cd /workspace
mkdir -p .ddev/ldap-bootstrap
cp test_users.ldif .ddev/ldap-bootstrap/test_users.ldif
sed -i 's#- ../test_users.ldif:/container/service/slapd/assets/config/bootstrap/ldif/custom/test_users.ldif#- ./ldap-bootstrap:/container/service/slapd/assets/config/bootstrap/ldif/custom#' .ddev/docker-compose.ldap.yaml
grep -n "ldap-bootstrap\|volumes:" .ddev/docker-compose.ldap.yaml | head
su - ddevuser -c 'cd /workspace && ddev restart 2>&1' | tail -25; echo "EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
